So, my two best friends in high school were Paul and Nazi Mike. Nazi Mike was, as his name implies, a dyed in the wool Nazi. Swastika tattoos and the works. Paul, on the other hand, was a towering guy, black as coal and sporting a mohawk. Now, one would think that Mike and Paul would hate each other, but they were good friends. Paul had Mike's back when he would get hassled over the swastikas, Mike had Paul's back when we were at a show with a bunch of skins. There were always good hearted debates between the two.

So, I should be able to offer some insight here...but I can't. I never was able to figure it out. I would ask them, and the closest they came to introspection was "well, it's different with him. He's one of the good ones."

I don't know. What I do know is that as the years went by, Nazi Mike became less and less of a Nazi. Paul became more relaxed about race issues. Last I heard, Mike had given up racism for good. (Shit. It's been twenty years since I saw those knuckleheads. I should search for them on Facebook)

Seems to me the best reason not to dismiss someone for hateful views isn't just the reason of human decency. It's that our hearts are changed by love and not by scolding. You hear stories of former Klan members, and their epiphany came not from people yelling at them, but by people showing compassion and friendship. Perhaps the fact that we've reviled racists so much is why there's so little change. Damned if I know.
